claim: A colorful cosmic nebula churns slowly, clouds of violet and rose lit from within with dark dust lanes and a scatter of soft stars.

q1_defects.answer: Nothing visibly broken, misaligned, cut off, or glitchy. The volume is a centered, organic, soft-edged cloud over the correct alpha-0 dark surround; no slab/shelf banding, no tile lattice, no mirror seam, no jagged edges, no blow-out. All bandingScores sit well under the 0.25 visible-banding line (0.171-0.195). Zero console or network errors.
evidence: metrics: idle bandingScore=0.178, play-1..3 bandingScore=0.177, max across all 13 frames = brightness-high 0.195 (< 0.25 threshold)

q2_reads_as.answer: Yes — it reads as exactly what it claims. idle.png and play-3.png show violet/rose clouds with a brighter rose-pink core lit from within, dark dust lanes cutting between the lobes, and a scatter of small soft stars. Measured dominant hue 261-267 deg at sat 0.40-0.45 is squarely violet (coolFrac 0.82-0.86, warmFrac 0), matching the violet-and-rose claim. Photoreal bar passed: smooth volumetric falloff, no Minecraft blockiness, bandingScore 0.177 on play frames.
evidence: metrics: play-3 effHue=262 effSat=0.44 coolFrac=0.84 warmFrac=0; bandingScore=0.177

q3_discoverable.answer: Mostly yes. 'scale' visibly and sensibly reworks the cloud (low = smooth blobby lobes with sparse large stars, satPixels 41616; high = finer wispy detail with a denser starfield, stdev 9->11.3). 'brightness' sweeps dim->glowing exactly as labeled (meanLuma 8.3->10.8, effRGB blue channel 14.5->52.9). 'speed' shows no visible difference between its three static frames (changed=false) — but speed changes churn RATE, which a single static frame per setting structurally cannot show for a cloud whose churn delta is only 0.18-0.2/frame; evidence is inconclusive rather than proof of a dead control. Flagged for a temporal recapture.
evidence: control: scale low->high changed=true, satPixels 41616->4662, stdev 10.2->11.3
control: brightness low->high changed=true, meanLuma 8.3->10.8, effRGB [7.5,8,14.5]->[41.1,31.5,52.9]
control: speed low/mid/high changed=false (static frames identical; temporal-rate change not measurable by this capture)

q4_responsive.answer: Responsive, not janky. The cloud is visibly in motion across the play phase — play-3 shows the core brightened and the lower lobe churned versus idle (frameDeltaMag 1.01). Control applies land in ~0.6s consistently (583-597ms) with no stalls. Only 1 of 3 controls shows no static-frame change (below the rubric's '>1 control with no change = dead' line), and the other two change the frame decisively.
evidence: metrics: play-1 frameDeltaMag=0.18, play-2=0.2, play-3=1.01 (visible churn)
control: latencyMs 583-597 across all 9 sweep applies

q5_net.answer: PLEASED. 'That looks like a real nebula photo come to life — soft purple clouds with a glowing pink heart, dark gaps, little stars, and the sliders actually reshape and brighten it.' The only nit is I couldn't see the Speed slider do anything in a still frame, and it could default a touch brighter — neither would stop me using it.
evidence: metrics: play-3 effHue=262 effSat=0.44 bandingScore=0.177, consoleErrors=[]

flags.note: Speed control unverifiable from static frames: low/mid/high captures are pixel-identical (changed=false). Because speed alters churn RATE and the churn delta is only ~0.2/frame, single-frame capture cannot distinguish working-slow from dead. Recommend a paired-delta recapture (two frames N ms apart at speed=low vs speed=high, compare frameDeltaMag) to prove the control live.
flags.evidence: control: speed low/mid/high changed=false, satPixels 4421/4419/4400 (noise-level); nebula/after/control-speed-low.png vs nebula/after/control-speed-high.png visually identical

flags.note: Default presentation is on the dim side (meanLuma 9.3, effRGB [27.4,21.4,38.3] at idle) — visible and correctly composed against the alpha-0 surround, but a slightly punchier default would read better on bright displays. Taste call, not a defect; brightness-high proves headroom exists.
flags.evidence: metrics: idle meanLuma=9.3 effRGB=[27.4,21.4,38.3]; control-brightness-high meanLuma=10.8 effRGB=[41.1,31.5,52.9]
